title: LRU Cache With list and unordered_map
statement:
A **least-recently-used** cache holds at most `capacity` entries; when a
new key would exceed that, the entry that was touched longest ago is
evicted. Both reading and writing a key count as "touching" it.

## The type

```
struct LruCache
{
    int capacity;                                            // >= 1
    std::list<std::pair<int, int>> order;                    // (key, value), most recent first
    std::unordered_map<int, std::list<std::pair<int, int>>::iterator> index;
};
```

`order` and `index` start empty. Keep them consistent: `index[key]` must
point at the node for `key` in `order`.

## Your functions

```
int  Get(LruCache& cache, int key);               // value, or -1 if absent
void Put(LruCache& cache, int key, int value);
```

- `Get` returns the value and marks `key` most recently used; a missing
  key returns `-1` and changes nothing.
- `Put` inserts or **updates** `key`, marks it most recently used, and, if
  the cache now holds more than `capacity` entries, evicts the least
  recently used one.

## Watch out

- **`Get` must refresh recency.** A cache whose reads do not reorder
  anything evicts a hot key as soon as enough new ones arrive.
- **Updating an existing key must not grow the cache or evict anything** --
  it replaces the value and moves the node to the front.
- **`list::splice` moves a node in O(1) without invalidating iterators**,
  so the iterators stored in `index` stay valid. Erasing and re-inserting
  would work but leave a stale iterator in the map unless you refresh it.
- When evicting, **remove the key from `index` as well** as from `order`.

tests.description: Putting 3 into a full cache of 2 evicts key 1.

tests.name: a get protects a key from eviction
tests.stdin:
2 6
put 1 1
put 2 2
get 1
put 3 3
get 2
get 1
tests.description: Reading 1 makes 2 the oldest, so 2 is evicted when 3 arrives.

tests.name: updating a key neither grows nor evicts
tests.stdin:
2 6
put 1 1
put 2 2
put 1 11
put 3 3
get 2
get 1
tests.description: The update refreshes key 1, so key 2 is the one evicted.
